## Description {#details}

A base class for a doubly linked list.

A pair of uninitialised pointers to the <b>next</b> and <b>previous</b> list elements, plus a set of simple (some inlined) methods to access the pointers.


:::info
Both the regular and the statically allocated list elements are derived from this class.
:::

### double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base() {#a414a3b580f22c9e5b528748321f444bf}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base::double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base ()</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Construct an uninitialised list node.

This must be an empty constructor, that does not touch the pointers, but leaves them unchanged.

For statically initialised lists, this means a pair of <code>nullptr</code> pointers.

For regular lists, the constructor of the derived class will handle the initialisations.

### initialize&#95;once() {#a19d5ef00655b74ec23dee3a4acb08513}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>void micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base::initialize&#95;once (void)</>}>
Initialize the list only at first run.

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>


<SectionUser title="Returns">
Nothing.
</SectionUser>

If the statically allocated list is still in the initial <em>uninitialised</em> state (with both pointers <code>nullptr</code>), initialise the list to the empty state, with both pointers pointing to itself.

For non-statically initialised lists, this method is ineffective, since the node is always initialised at construct time.


:::info
This method must be manually called for statically allocated list before inserting elements, or performing any other operations.
:::
